posts.notes: Ninth cycle overall, fired manually by direct user request ('push posts everywhere') after discovering the nightly crons had silently expired (auto-expire after 7 days) and the pipeline had been quiet since 09-22. Recreated the nightly cron same day. linkedin-bot.py --post exited 1 on the usual toast false-negative; confirmed genuinely live via the Browser pane -- post #1, timestamped 'now', full matching text. Page now at 4 followers. scheduled_slot recorded as null and NOT marked as a valid timing trial -- this was an immediate manual fire, not a slot the exploration algorithm chose.

Tenth cycle overall, fired via /orl-publish --fire (Skill tool, session-based, no API key) at its scheduled 18:00 slot -- first fully on-time /orl-publish --fire execution logged since the pipeline moved to session-native CronCreate scheduling. linkedin-bot.py --post exited 1 on the usual toast false-negative; confirmed genuinely live via the Browser pane -- post #1 on company/144914968/admin/page-posts/published/, timestamped 'now', full matching text, dated 9/26/2026. Page at 4 followers. analytics_checked_at left null -- tomorrow night's /orl-timing --log-previous fills it in and marks the 18:00 slot as tried. UPDATE 2026-09-27 (log-previous check): linkedin-bot.py --analytics returned 96 impressions / 1 click -- identical to the ALREADY-LOGGED 2026-09-25 entry. Cross-verified via the Browser pane on company/144914968/admin/page-posts/published/: this post (Feed post #1, 6h old at check time) currently shows NO "Organic impressions" summary line at all, while Feed post #3 (the 2026-09-25 post) is the one showing "Organic impressions: 96" -- confirmed by expanding its own Preview results panel, exact match to the script output. This is a NEW confirmed bug in linkedin-bot.py --analytics: it appears to pick the first post with a non-zero/rendered impressions panel rather than strictly the newest post, so a very fresh post with ~0 impressions gets skipped and the prior post's numbers get misattributed to it. NOT writing the 96/1 numbers here -- they belong to the 09-25 entry, not this one. Leaving analytics_checked_at null so a future --log-previous run picks this entry up again once it has genuinely accumulated impressions of its own; the 18:00 slot is NOT being marked as tried in state.json this cycle to avoid polluting timing-intelligence with wrong data. Flagged to user -- this is a distinct bug from UB's long-standing all-null --analytics parser bug.
